size_ceiling.model_context_source: read from the model's own GGUF header (model_header)
size_ceiling.why: the largest size 8192 comes from --sizes [4096, 8192]; it plus n_predict 16 fits the 16384-token per-slot ctx with 8176 tokens spare (--parallel 1), and the model's trained context read from its own GGUF header is 131072: the ceiling is a choice of what this run has to measure, not a model or ctx limit; a size that did not fit would be refused above, never truncated

provenance.argv_facts_source: parsed back out of the argv every arm receives (flags_from_argv), asserted equal per arm and against the intended flags before the first engine
provenance.sleep_idle_note: short so the release lands inside the run; the app ships 300
provenance.max_load_note: gate on the 1-minute load average, checked before any engine starts; 0 disables it and would be recorded as 0.0
provenance.warm_threshold_kind: RULE - the line this verdict draws, not a measured datum
provenance.wall_times_note: wall times are measurements of this machine at nice 10 under whatever else it was doing, not performance promises
provenance.invariant_note: contention-invariant: token counts, cache_n, file bytes. NOT invariant: prompt_ms, save_ms, every wall - they move with loadavg_before (recorded above and below) and are labelled wherever they are quoted
provenance.refusal_semantics: EXIT 0 means the artifact was written. A measurement that is invalid is refused INSIDE the artifact, not by the exit code: the arm carries measured=false with its blockers and the conclusion begins 'no verdict: ...' - this harness's deliverable is the evidence of WHY a run failed, and a non-zero exit would make that record look like a crash and invite a re-run that overwrites it. The two gates are the exceptions: --max-load and the headroom check exit non-zero BEFORE anything is measured, and write no artifact

ctx_measurement_caveat.note: largest size 8192 + n_predict 16 fits ctx_size 16384 (8176 tokens spare) and also fits the app's default context 65536 (57328 spare): no comparability caveat; per-token figures are ctx-independent by the committed evidence (same 53,352 B/token at ctx 8192 and ctx 16384).

disk_law.formula: bytes = per_layer_bpt x (layer_full x tokens + 2 x layer_windowed x min(tokens, window))

verdict.conclusion: after a real release the saved chats came back warm and the no-file controls stayed cold, so the warmth travelled with the file. Numbers: 4096 tokens: saved cache_n=4091/4096 n_restored=4111 restore=683.92ms (resident 18.27ms, reload est. 604.1ms), control cache_n=0/4096; 8192 tokens: saved cache_n=8187/8192 n_restored=8207 restore=695.63ms (resident 22.55ms, reload est. 612.6ms), control cache_n=0/8192 | disk curve: (a) bytes/token: 4096 tokens -> 125012200 B = 30521 B/token; 8192 tokens -> 156272872 B = 19076 B/token (marginal 4096->8192: 7632 B/token); the 600->1900 base was 53352 B/token, the q8_0 full-KV arithmetic from the model's own GGUF header is 30464 B/token. THE KNEE LIES BELOW THE SMALLEST SIZE MEASURED HERE (4096 tokens): that interval's marginal already reads 7632 B/token against the 53352 below-window base, so the 2048-token window was crossed between 1900 (the base's upper end, measured in the companion 600/1900 artifact) and 4096 tokens. THAT INTERVAL IS ALREADY BEYOND THE KNEE: its marginal 7632 B/token IS the post-window slope - the 14 full layers x 544 = 7616 B/token (measured 7632) - so the slope is flat past the knee and NO further bend is announced in this range. (b) benefit per size: 4096 tokens: 2120.497 ms cold re-prefill vs 52.95 ms warm -> 2067.5 ms avoided, 4091/4096 tokens reused; 8192 tokens: 4592.412 ms cold re-prefill vs 55.744 ms warm -> 4536.7 ms avoided, 8187/8192 tokens reused - the MILLISECOND half is this machine at this load (contention-dependent, not a promise); the invariant half is the token count and the byte counts above; the benefit grows about LINEARLY with the token count (0.505 -> 0.554 ms avoided per token, 4096 -> 8192 tokens). (c) the plan derives ~218 MB per 4096-token chat (~53 KB/token x 4096): MUST BE CORRECTED - measured 125012200 B (125.0 MB, -42.7 % against the derivation); the citable figure is 125.0 MB. (d) at 8192 tokens there is NO excess: the file sits 11388 B/token BELOW the header's full-KV arithmetic, which is what the 2048-token window capping the windowed layers does to a file. The positive excess exists only BELOW the window; it is measured and attributed in the companion 600/1900-token artifact (dev/results/unload-restore-release), not re-derived from this one. (e) the law read from the model's own header - 2048-token window, 14 full + 42 windowed layers from the boot lines, 544 B/layer/token, layers sum to 56 blocks (True): 4096: predicted 124780544 B vs measured 125012200 B (+0.19 %); 8192: predicted 155975680 B vs measured 156272872 B (+0.19 %) -> the law HOLDS within 0.19 % at every size (f) THE OWNER NUMBER IS A DERIVATION IN THIS ARTIFACT: no chat of 65536 tokens was measured here (sizes: 4096, 8192); the law above puts it at 592707584 bytes = 592.7 MB per saved chat - DECLARED as arithmetic, measured in dev/results/unload-restore-app-context/
